meta.description: Batch program that reads all credit card account records sequentially and distributes account data into multiple output files in different formats for downstream processing and reporting.
meta.process_description: The program performs a full sequential read of the master credit card account file and, for each account, writes the account data to three different output files: a flat sequential file containing full account details, an array-structured file containing multi-occurrence balance and debit data, and a variable-length record file containing two record types (a short status record and a longer financial summary record). During processing, the card reissue date is reformatted via a date conversion utility (COBDATFT) before being written to the output file. The program logs all account fields to the system console for audit/tracing purposes and abends with an error if any file operation fails.

files.ACCTFILE: Master credit card account indexed file — the source of all account records processed by this program
files.OUTFILE: Sequential flat output file containing full account details (balances, limits, dates, status, group) for each account
files.ARRYFILE: Sequential array-structured output file containing account ID with multiple sets of current balance and cycle debit figures per account, used for multi-period or multi-scenario downstream processing
files.VBRCFILE: Variable-length record output file containing two record types per account: a short record (account ID + active status) and a longer record (account ID + balance + credit limit + reissue year), supporting downstream systems requiring variable-format input

business_rules: Every account in the master account file is processed — this is a full-file extract with no filtering by account status or balance.

If the current cycle debit amount for an account is zero, a default value of 2525.00 is substituted in the flat output file, suggesting a minimum or placeholder debit figure is required by downstream systems.

The card reissue date must be reformatted using the COBDATFT date conversion utility (type 2 input, type 2 output) before being written to the output file, ensuring a consistent date format for downstream consumers.

The array output file always populates exactly three balance/debit occurrences per account: occurrences 1 and 2 use the actual current balance with hardcoded debit values (1005.00 and 1525.00), while occurrence 3 uses hardcoded negative values (-1025.00 balance, -2500.00 debit), suggesting test data generation or scenario modelling rather than live production data.

Two variable-length records are written per account to the VBRCFILE: a 12-byte short record (ID + status) and a 39-byte longer record (ID + balance + credit limit + reissue year), supporting downstream systems with different data granularity needs.
Any file I/O error (open, read, or write) on any of the four files causes an immediate program abend, ensuring no partial or corrupt output is silently produced.
All account field values are written to the system console log for each record processed, providing a full audit trail of the batch run.

Checks whether the file status code returned by the last file operation is non-numeric, which would indicate an abnormal or system-level file error rather than a standard COBOL file condition.
Also checks whether the file status indicates a hardware or operating-system-level error (status codes beginning with '9' signal serious, non-standard file failures).
Captures the first character of the file status code into the display buffer so the full error code can be assembled for console output.
Clears a working numeric area to zero in preparation for converting the second part of the file status code into a displayable numeric format.
Places the second character of the file status code into the right-hand portion of the conversion area, ready for numeric interpretation.
Converts the raw binary representation of the second status character into a numeric value that can be displayed meaningfully to operations staff.
Writes the fully assembled abnormal file status code to the system console, allowing operators to identify the exact nature of the file failure.
Begins the alternative path for standard, numeric file status codes that do not represent system-level failures.
Initialises the display buffer with zeros so that any unused positions in the status display field are blank rather than containing stale data.
Inserts the standard two-character file status code into the correct position within the display buffer for accurate console reporting.
Writes the formatted standard file status code to the system console, providing the operations team with the specific file condition that occurred.
Closes the conditional logic block that handles both abnormal and standard file status scenarios.
Marks the end of this diagnostic routine and returns control to the calling paragraph.

variables.name: FD-ACCTFILE-REC
variables.description: File buffer record for the master credit card account file (ACCTFILE). Represents the raw layout used to physically read each account record from the indexed master file before its data is mapped into working storage for processing.

variables.name: FD-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The unique 11-digit account number as read directly from the master account file. This is the primary key used to identify which credit card account record has just been read from disk.

variables.name: FD-ACCT-DATA
variables.description: The remaining 289 bytes of raw account data following the account ID in the physical file record (balances, limits, dates, status, group, etc.). This bulk field holds all other account attributes before they are parsed into named working-storage fields for business processing.

variables.name: OUT-ACCT-REC
variables.description: The output record layout written to the sequential flat output file (OUTFILE). Represents a fully formatted account snapshot — including balances, limits, dates, status and group — that downstream reporting and processing systems will consume.

variables.name: OUT-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The unique 11-digit credit card account number written to the flat output file. Allows downstream systems to uniquely identify which account each output record belongs to.

variables.name: OUT-ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS
variables.description: A single-character flag written to the flat output file indicating whether the credit card account is currently active or inactive. Downstream systems use this to determine whether the account is eligible for transactions, statements or other processing.

variables.name: OUT-ACCT-CURR-BAL
variables.description: The current outstanding balance on the credit card account, written to the flat output file. Represents the total amount the cardholder currently owes, used by downstream systems for billing, risk assessment and reporting.

variables.name: OUT-ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT
variables.description: The maximum credit limit authorised for the account, written to the flat output file. Downstream systems use this to calculate available credit, enforce spending controls and produce limit utilisation reports.

variables.name: OUT-ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT
variables.description: The maximum cash advance credit limit authorised for the account, written to the flat output file. Downstream systems use this to control and report on the cardholder's ability to withdraw cash against their credit line.

variables.name: OUT-ACCT-OPEN-DATE
variables.description: The date the credit card account was originally opened, written to the flat output file. Used by downstream systems for customer tenure analysis, anniversary processing and regulatory reporting.

variables.name: OUT-ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE
variables.description: The expiry date of the credit card associated with the account, written to the flat output file. Downstream systems use this to identify cards approaching expiry and trigger card renewal or replacement workflows.

variables.name: OUT-ACCT-REISSUE-DATE
variables.description: The reformatted card reissue date written to the flat output file. This date has been converted via the COBDATFT date utility to a consistent format, indicating when the card was or is scheduled to be reissued, supporting downstream card management and fulfilment systems.

variables.name: OUT-ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT
variables.description: The total credits posted to the account during the current billing cycle, written to the flat output file. Downstream systems use this for cycle-to-date statement generation, payment reconciliation and balance calculations.

variables.name: OUT-ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT
variables.description: The total debits posted to the account during the current billing cycle, written to the flat output file. If the actual cycle debit is zero, a default placeholder value of 2525.00 is substituted, ensuring downstream systems always receive a non-zero debit figure for processing integrity.

variables.name: OUT-ACCT-GROUP-ID
variables.description: The customer group or portfolio segment identifier written to the flat output file. Downstream systems use this to segment accounts by product type, risk tier or customer category for targeted reporting and portfolio management.

variables.name: ARR-ARRAY-REC
variables.description: The output record layout written to the array-structured output file (ARRYFILE). Represents an account with multiple balance and debit occurrences per record, supporting downstream multi-period or multi-scenario processing and modelling.

variables.name: ARR-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The unique 11-digit credit card account number written to the array output file. Identifies which account the multiple balance/debit scenario occurrences in the same record belong to.

variables.name: ARR-ACCT-BAL
variables.description: A repeating group of up to five balance and debit pairs per account record in the array output file. Each occurrence represents a distinct balance/debit scenario or time period, allowing downstream systems to process multiple financial snapshots for the same account in a single record. Only three of the five occurrences are populated by this program.

variables.name: ARR-ACCT-CURR-BAL
variables.description: The account balance figure for one scenario or period occurrence in the array output record. Occurrences 1 and 2 carry the actual current balance; occurrence 3 carries a hardcoded negative value (-1025.00), indicating a test or modelled scenario rather than a live balance.

variables.name: ARR-ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT
variables.description: The cycle debit figure for one scenario or period occurrence in the array output record. Occurrence 1 uses a hardcoded value of 1005.00, occurrence 2 uses 1525.00, and occurrence 3 uses -2500.00, indicating these are test or scenario-modelling values rather than live transaction data.

variables.name: ARR-FILLER
variables.description: A 4-byte padding field at the end of the array output record. Ensures the record meets the required fixed length for the ARRYFILE, with no business data content.

variables.name: VBR-REC
variables.description: The generic 80-byte working buffer used to stage variable-length records before they are written to the VBRCFILE. The actual content and byte length written are controlled by WS-RECD-LEN, allowing either the short 12-byte record (account ID + status) or the longer 39-byte record (account ID + balance + limit + reissue year) to be output for each account.

variables.name: ACCTFILE-STATUS
variables.description: The two-character file status code returned by the operating system after every I/O operation on the master account file (ACCTFILE). Used to detect and respond to read errors or end-of-file conditions, triggering an immediate program abend if an unexpected status is received.

variables.name: ACCTFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the ACCTFILE I/O status code. A value of '0' generally indicates success; any other value signals a file error that will cause the batch program to abend immediately.

variables.name: ACCTFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the ACCTFILE I/O status code. Combined with ACCTFILE-STAT1, provides the specific reason code for any file error encountered when reading the master account file.

variables.name: OUTFILE-STATUS
variables.description: The two-character file status code returned after every I/O operation on the sequential flat output file (OUTFILE). Used to detect write errors and trigger an immediate abend to prevent partial or corrupt output from being silently produced.

variables.name: OUTFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the OUTFILE I/O status code. Indicates the general success or failure category of the most recent write operation to the flat account output file.

variables.name: OUTFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the OUTFILE I/O status code. Provides the specific error detail code for any failure encountered when writing account records to the flat output file.

variables.name: ARRYFILE-STATUS
variables.description: The two-character file status code returned after every I/O operation on the array-structured output file (ARRYFILE). Used to detect write errors and trigger an immediate abend to protect the integrity of the multi-scenario account output.

variables.name: ARRYFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the ARRYFILE I/O status code. Indicates the general success or failure category of the most recent write operation to the array output file.

variables.name: ARRYFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the ARRYFILE I/O status code. Provides the specific error detail code for any failure encountered when writing multi-scenario account records to the array output file.

variables.name: VBRCFILE-STATUS
variables.description: The two-character file status code returned after every I/O operation on the variable-length record output file (VBRCFILE). Used to detect write errors and trigger an immediate abend to ensure no partial variable-length records are silently written.

variables.name: VBRCFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the VBRCFILE I/O status code. Indicates the general success or failure category of the most recent write operation to the variable-length record output file.

variables.name: VBRCFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the VBRCFILE I/O status code. Provides the specific error detail code for any failure encountered when writing variable-length account records to the VBRCFILE.

variables.name: IO-STATUS
variables.description: A general-purpose two-character I/O status code holder used to consolidate and evaluate file status results across all four output files. Supports centralised error checking logic that determines whether to continue processing or abend the batch run.

variables.name: IO-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the consolidated I/O status code. Used in error evaluation routines to determine the general category of any file operation result across the batch program.

variables.name: IO-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the consolidated I/O status code. Provides the specific reason code used alongside IO-STAT1 to diagnose and report file errors during the batch run.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-BINARY
variables.description: A two-byte binary numeric field used to hold and manipulate I/O status codes in their raw binary form. Allows the program to inspect individual bytes of a status code by overlaying it with the TWO-BYTES-ALPHA redefinition, supporting precise error diagnosis.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-ALPHA
variables.description: An alphanumeric redefinition of TWO-BYTES-BINARY that allows the same two bytes to be read as individual characters. Enables the program to inspect the left and right bytes of a binary status code separately for error handling and reporting.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-LEFT
variables.description: The left (first) byte of the binary I/O status code when viewed as characters. Used in error handling routines to extract and evaluate the high-order byte of a file status result.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-RIGHT
variables.description: The right (second) byte of the binary I/O status code when viewed as characters. Used in error handling routines to extract and evaluate the low-order byte of a file status result.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-04
variables.description: A structured working-storage area used to decompose and display a numeric I/O status code for error reporting. Splits the status into a single leading digit and a three-digit detail code to support formatted error messages in the batch run log.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-0401
variables.description: The leading single digit of a numeric I/O status code, initialised to zero. Represents the high-level status category (e.g. 0 = success, 1 = end of file, 9 = system error) used in error reporting when a file operation fails.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-0403
variables.description: The three-digit detail portion of a numeric I/O status code, initialised to zero. Provides the specific reason code within the status category, used to produce precise error messages in the batch run log when a file operation fails.

variables.name: APPL-RESULT
variables.description: A signed numeric result code used to capture the outcome of file I/O operations and utility calls (such as the date conversion utility). Evaluated against the APPL-AOK and APPL-EOF condition names to determine whether processing should continue, end normally or abend.

variables.name: APPL-AOK
variables.description: A condition name that is true when APPL-RESULT equals zero, indicating a file or utility operation completed successfully. Used throughout the program to confirm that reading, writing and date conversion operations succeeded before continuing to the next account.

variables.name: APPL-EOF
variables.description: A condition name that is true when APPL-RESULT equals 16, indicating that the end of the master account file has been reached. When this condition is detected, the program stops reading and proceeds to close all output files and end the batch run.

variables.name: END-OF-FILE
variables.description: A flag that controls the main account processing loop. Initialised to 'N' (not at end of file), it is set to 'Y' when the last account record has been read from the master file, signalling the program to stop reading and begin its end-of-job closedown.

variables.name: ABCODE
variables.description: The abend code passed to the system when the program terminates abnormally due to a file I/O error. Ensures that any failure in reading the master account file or writing to any output file results in a clearly identifiable abnormal termination code for operations and support teams.

variables.name: TIMING
variables.description: A binary numeric field used to pass a timing or delay parameter to the abend utility routine. Controls how the abnormal termination is handled at the system level when a critical file error forces the batch program to stop.

variables.name: WS-RECD-LEN
variables.description: The actual byte length of the variable-length record to be written to the VBRCFILE. Set to 12 before writing the short record (account ID + active status) and to 39 before writing the longer record (account ID + balance + credit limit + reissue year), controlling exactly how many bytes each downstream variable-format record contains.

variables.name: VBRC-REC1
variables.description: The short variable-length record layout written first for each account to the VBRCFILE. Contains only the account ID and active status (12 bytes total), providing downstream systems that need minimal account identification data with a compact record format.

variables.name: VB1-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The unique 11-digit credit card account number in the short variable-length record. Identifies the account for downstream systems consuming the compact VBRCFILE record format.

variables.name: VB1-ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS
variables.description: The single-character active/inactive status flag in the short variable-length record. Allows downstream systems reading the compact 12-byte VBRCFILE record to quickly determine whether the account is currently active without needing the full account detail record.

variables.name: VBRC-REC2
variables.description: The longer variable-length record layout written second for each account to the VBRCFILE. Contains the account ID, current balance, credit limit and reissue year (39 bytes total), providing downstream systems that require financial and card lifecycle data with a richer record format.

variables.name: VB2-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The unique 11-digit credit card account number in the longer variable-length record. Links the financial and card reissue data in this record to the correct account for downstream systems consuming the VBRCFILE.

variables.name: VB2-ACCT-CURR-BAL
variables.description: The current outstanding balance on the credit card account, included in the longer variable-length record. Provides downstream systems consuming the 39-byte VBRCFILE record with the cardholder's current debt position.

variables.name: VB2-ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT
variables.description: The maximum credit limit authorised for the account, included in the longer variable-length record. Allows downstream systems consuming the 39-byte VBRCFILE record to calculate available credit and enforce limit controls.

variables.name: VB2-ACCT-REISSUE-YYYY
variables.description: The four-digit year extracted from the reformatted card reissue date, included in the longer variable-length record. Provides downstream systems with the year in which the card was or is scheduled to be reissued, supporting card lifecycle management and renewal planning.

variables.name: WS-ACCT-REISSUE-DATE
variables.description: A working-storage area used to hold and parse the reformatted card reissue date returned by the COBDATFT date conversion utility. Provides a structured layout from which individual date components (such as the reissue year) can be extracted for inclusion in the variable-length output record.

variables.name: WS-ACCT-REISSUE-YYYY
variables.description: The four-digit year component of the credit card reissue date, extracted after the date conversion utility (COBDATFT) reformats the raw reissue date from the account record. This year value is used when constructing the reissue date written to the variable-length output file (VBRCFILE), ensuring downstream systems receive the reissue year in a consistent, separated format.

variables.name: WS-FILLER-1
variables.description: A single-character separator (typically a hyphen or slash) positioned between the year and month components of the reformatted card reissue date. This separator ensures the reissue date is written in a human-readable, standardised date format (e.g. YYYY-MM-DD) that downstream systems and reporting consumers expect.

variables.name: WS-ACCT-REISSUE-MM
variables.description: The two-digit month component of the credit card reissue date, extracted after the date conversion utility reformats the raw reissue date from the account record. This month value forms part of the structured reissue date written to output files, allowing downstream systems to identify the specific month in which the card was or is due to be reissued.

variables.name: WS-FILLER-2
variables.description: A single-character separator (typically a hyphen or slash) positioned between the month and day components of the reformatted card reissue date. Together with WS-FILLER-1, this ensures the reissue date is presented in a consistent, delimited format (e.g. YYYY-MM-DD) across all output files produced by the batch run.

variables.name: WS-ACCT-REISSUE-DD
variables.description: The two-digit day component of the credit card reissue date, extracted after the date conversion utility reformats the raw reissue date from the account record. This day value completes the structured reissue date written to output files, giving downstream systems the full calendar date on which the card was or is scheduled to be reissued.

variables.name: WS-REISSUE-DATE
variables.description: A 10-character consolidated view of the fully reformatted credit card reissue date, overlaying the same memory as the individual year, separator, month, separator, and day components. This single contiguous field allows the program to write the complete reissue date (e.g. 2024-08-15) as one atomic value to the output files, particularly the variable-length record file (VBRCFILE), without needing to concatenate the individual components at write time.

paragraphs.name: 1000-ACCTFILE-GET-NEXT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph drives the core processing loop by reading the next credit card account from the master file and, if successful, orchestrating the full sequence of output writes across all three downstream files. It also handles end-of-file detection and abends immediately on any unexpected read error to prevent silent data loss.

paragraphs.name: 1100-DISPLAY-ACCT-RECORD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph writes a complete snapshot of each credit card account's key attributes to the system console log, providing a full audit trail of every account processed during the batch run. It ensures that operators and auditors can verify exactly what data was read from the master file for each account.

paragraphs.name: 1300-POPUL-ACCT-RECORD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph assembles the full account record for the flat sequential output file by copying all key account attributes from the master file, applying a mandatory date format conversion to the card reissue date, and substituting a default debit figure when no current-cycle debit activity exists.

paragraphs.name: 1350-WRITE-ACCT-RECORD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph writes a fully populated account record to the flat sequential output file, which downstream systems use for reporting and further processing. It enforces strict data integrity by immediately aborting the entire batch job if the write operation fails, preventing any silent or partial output.

paragraphs.name: 1400-POPUL-ARRAY-RECORD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph constructs the array-structured output record for each account by populating three balance/debit scenario slots. Two slots use the account's real current balance paired with hardcoded debit figures, while a third slot contains fixed negative values, suggesting this output is used for scenario modelling or test data generation rather than live production reporting.

paragraphs.name: 1450-WRITE-ARRY-RECORD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph writes the array-structured account record — containing multiple sets of balance and debit figures — to the multi-period output file. If the write operation fails for any reason, the program immediately logs the error and abends to prevent corrupt or incomplete output from reaching downstream systems.

paragraphs.name: 1500-POPUL-VBRC-RECORD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph prepares two variable-length output records per account for downstream systems requiring different levels of data granularity: a short record containing only the account identifier and active/inactive status, and a longer record containing the account identifier, current outstanding balance, authorised credit limit, and card reissue year.

paragraphs.name: 1550-WRITE-VB1-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Writes a short 12-byte summary record to the variable-length output file, containing only the account identifier and active/inactive status flag, to satisfy downstream systems that require a lightweight status-only view of each account. If the write fails for any reason, the batch run is immediately halted to prevent incomplete or corrupt output from reaching downstream consumers.

paragraphs.name: 1575-WRITE-VB2-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Writes the longer of the two variable-length records to the variable-format output file, containing the full financial summary for an account (account ID, current balance, credit limit, and reissue year) in a fixed 39-byte format. This record supports downstream systems that require detailed financial data at a granular level.

paragraphs.name: 0000-ACCTFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the master credit card account file in preparation for the batch extract run. If the file cannot be opened successfully, the program immediately abends to prevent any downstream output being produced without source data.

paragraphs.name: 2000-OUTFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the flat sequential output file that will receive full account details for downstream processing and reporting. If the file cannot be opened, the program immediately abends to prevent any partial or silent data loss.

paragraphs.name: 3000-ARRFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the array-structured output file ready to receive multi-period balance and debit data for each account. If the file cannot be opened, the program immediately abends to prevent any partial or missing output from reaching downstream systems.

paragraphs.name: 4000-VBRFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the variable-length record output file in preparation for writing two types of account records per account (a short status record and a longer financial summary record). If the file cannot be opened, the program immediately abends to prevent any downstream system from receiving incomplete or missing data.

paragraphs.name: 9000-ACCTFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the master credit card account file at the end of batch processing, ensuring all data is flushed and the file is properly released. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program immediately abends to prevent data integrity issues and silent failures.

paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles unrecoverable processing failures by immediately terminating the batch program in a controlled abend, ensuring that any downstream systems or operators are clearly alerted to a critical error rather than receiving silent, incomplete, or corrupted output.

paragraphs.name: 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph formats and displays a human-readable file operation status code to the system console whenever a file I/O event occurs, supporting the audit trail and enabling operators or support staff to diagnose file processing failures during the batch run.
